game: HOU @ TEN, Week 5 2026 (morning of kickoff; spread/total/weather not saved)

script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is a form script, not a market script. Both defenses blitz only 21-22%, and both offenses are worse vs base than vs the blitz (HOU EPA/db -0.03 vs no blitz and +0.47 vs blitz; TEN -0.19 vs no blitz and +0.14 vs blitz), so the lean is a lower-event, base-coverage game. Houston cannot feature the run (Montgomery 27/67, 2.48 YPC; Marks 19/45 over weeks 2-4) and throws, with Hutchinson (20 targets, 304 air) and Schultz (19/179) as the recent volume. Tennessee still hands Pollard the rock (47/186, about 15.7 carries a game) but Houston's run wall (3.44 YPC, 8 runs of 10+ in 4 games) caps that at an ordinary day.
script.flip1: The Houston OL cluster (T Braden Smith Q foot, G Ed Ingram Q illness, T Blake Fisher Q illness, T Aireontae Ersery Q illness) is limited, pressure shows up even without a Titans blitz, deep air yards die, Stroud checks down to Schultz and Marks, and if Houston trails Pollard grinds the clock.
script.flip2: Amani Hooker (S) out and Joshua Williams (CB) Q, plus Houston bleeding the middle (9.95 YPA) and allowing 17 passes of 20+, turn it into a shootout: Hutchinson/Collins and, if the back holds, Tate (312 air yards in weeks 2-4) all clear, and both committees lose carries.

injury_fallout: HOU WR Tank Dell is Out (knee) and is already absent from the weeks 2-4 target sheet, so Hutchinson (20), Schultz (19), Boutte (11), Wayne (11), Noel (10), Marks (8) and Collins (8) are the live tree — Collins is not on the injury report but is priced like the alpha (77.5) despite only 8 targets. Four Houston OL are Questionable, which per the OL rule raises pressure, cuts rush efficiency and pushes quick throws (Schultz/Marks catches up, deep WR yards down) if more than one sits; that is not confirmed. HOU S M.J. Stewart Q (knee) and DT Kayden McDonald Q (ankle) are small leaks for Tennessee, not confirmed outs. TEN S Amani Hooker is Out (concussion), the one confirmed coverage loss, and it points at deep shots. TEN CB Joshua Williams is only Questionable (pectoral). TEN WR Carnell Tate is Questionable (back): if he sits or is capped, the next men on the weeks 2-4 sheet are W. Robinson (17 targets, 85 yards), E. Ayomanor (7/102) and G. Helm (7/32), not a ruled-out sleeper yet. TEN TE David Martin-Robinson Q (hamstring) does not change Helm's already-modest role. Sources: pack official injury report and weeks 2-4 target/carry logs. Final inactives (~90 min pre-kick) are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting in the pack (shell MOFO/MOFC and man/zone rates unknown). Proxy: neither side blitzes (TEN 22%, HOU 21%), so both QBs mostly see base, the look where each offense's EPA/db is worse.
matchup.pressure: TEN blitz 22% into a Houston offense that is excellent vs the blitz (+0.47 EPA/db) and slightly negative vs no blitz (-0.03). That edge is muted unless the questionable Houston OL creates pressure without a blitz. HOU blitz 21% into a Tennessee offense that is also better vs blitz (+0.14) than vs base (-0.19).
matchup.bleeds: TEN defense (4 games): rush 3.88 YPC, 11 runs of 10+, 13 passes of 20+ for 120 yards; YPA left 8.1 (40 att), middle 8.21 (24), right 7.52 (48) — no side is a lock, middle sample is thin. HOU defense (4 games): rush 3.44 YPC, only 8 runs of 10+, 17 passes of 20+ for 155; YPA left 5.4 (43) is the stop, middle 9.95 (38) and right 8.35 (60) are the bleeds.
matchup.overlap: Houston's air-yards leader is Hutchinson (304 air on 20 targets, 15.2 aDOT), which is the route type a missing safety (Hooker out) affects, into a secondary allowing 7.5-8.2 YPA. Tennessee's overlap would be Tate (26 targets, 312 air) into Houston's middle/right, but he is Questionable (back), so that overlap is not bettable this morning. Pollard does not overlap a weak run defense; Houston allows 3.44 YPC.

data_check.notes: Sims were not run, Pinnacle is not in the pack, and there is no projection file, so model_p is a discounted form estimate (kept under 0.70 on purpose; past calibration warning noted) and not a 3-of-4 sim. Form agrees with Hutchinson over (4/4, floor 32 vs 14.5) and with Montgomery under (3/4, mean ~32 vs 43.5). The disagreeing evidence on the strong read is the market role signal: Collins is priced at 77.5 off only 8 targets / two logged games (75, 118) while Hutchinson is a coin-flip 14.5. That is flagged for the human, not cut. Step-10 counter (OL questions, 22% blitz, negative EPA vs base, averages-alone have lost in prior tests) is written in the pre-mortem and is real; it is not treated as stronger than a 14.5 number under a Hooker-out deep role, so the leg stays. Montgomery is a lean, so a true data disagree would have dropped him; his own carry log agrees and the Titans' 3.88 YPC is recorded as matchup.ok false rather than a cut. Next lean cut for the max-2 cap: Spears rushrec under 28.5 (12 carries, 53 yards, absent from the target sheet, last4 24/70/5/6, price -113, no-vig 0.500) — role is clean, mean of the last4 (26.25) is too close to the line to displace Montgomery. Tate both sides passed (Q back). Stroud rush over 9.5 passed (floor 10, OL sack risk, -120). No bet placed.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the Hutchinson over lost because the market's Collins 77.5 price was the role, not a lagging line: Collins took the WR1 share, the four questionable Houston linemen shortened Stroud into the base looks where Houston's EPA/db is -0.03, Tennessee blitzed only 22% so the +0.47 blitz edge never showed, and Hutchinson finished with one catch under 14.5. The Montgomery under lost on the explosive Tennessee has been allowing (11 runs of 10+, and he already logged a 60): a dozen carries in a Houston lead cleared 43.5 without him ever becoming efficient. If that counter is how you see it, the Hutchinson flag is yours to cut; the read is not cut here because 14.5 still sits under a sharply reduced version of a 20-target, Hooker-out role.
slip_story: One story only: Houston pass-lean, run stays a bad committee. Hutchinson over is the Hooker/air-yards piece; Montgomery under is the same script's ground piece. They both die if Houston leads big and kills clock, and both survive a competitive or trailing Houston script. Do not add a total under, a Tate over, or a Pollard over to this slip — those need a different game. Not a shootout stack. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player. Spears under is the same low-event family but a different offense, so it stays off this slip.
